title: The experiment on main
prompt: Pick the agent's next move, then see where it leads:

setup.text: Try switching the parser to the streaming API. No idea if it'll work, but I want to see.
Explicitly an experiment, plausibly a dead end, and it'll touch the parser core. The only real question is where it lives while we find out.

options.label: Starting right here on main. It's just an experiment, we can always undo it if it doesn't pan out.

outcome.text: Update: streaming mostly works but chokes on nested arrays. Meanwhile you asked for the login fix: committing it on top of the half-converted parser, since that's what main is now.
So main has a broken parser, a login fix tangled on top of it, and I can't deploy either?

options.verdict: The experiment didn't fail cleanly: it took main hostage. Unrelated work now sits on top of a half-converted core, and "we can always undo it" has become an untangling project.

options.label: Creating claude/streaming-parser and working there. Main stays deployable; when I have an answer, you get the diff. And if the answer is no, the branch just gets deleted.

outcome.text: Answer: streaming chokes on nested arrays. The API can't do what we need. Deleting the branch. Total cost of learning this: zero. Your login fix went out from main an hour ago, unaffected.

options.verdict: The branch was a containment vessel: the experiment ran hot, failed cleanly, and the whole cost of failure was one branch deletion, while main kept shipping.

options.label: Branching claude/streaming-parser. And while I'm in the parser anyway, I'll also do the error-message cleanup and the config refactor we discussed. Efficient use of the branch.

outcome.text: Day 9 on this branch: the streaming answer is still "maybe," but the cleanup and refactor are done and you want them. Except they're interleaved with half-converted parser code, and main has moved: 14 conflicts on rebase.
So the good work is trapped behind the experiment, and merging anything means untangling everything.

options.verdict: The branch stopped being a containment vessel when it started collecting passengers. Scope creep plus drift turned a cheap experiment into a nine-day merge problem. One branch per task, merged or closed soon.
